I'll attach the renewal summary and a draft SOW amendment. Tim — if you can confirm the PO path in your portal (single-line amendment vs new PO), we'll tailor the filenames and metadata for upload.

Hi Tim / Sarah — looping in billing details to reduce churn.

We prefer one of two approaches depending on your internal controls:
A) Amendment on existing PO: we apply pro-rated uplift as a separate line item referencing the original PO number — fastest for systems that support amendments.
B) New PO + reference: submit a new PO that references the existing contract and notes the term extension date. This is cleaner for teams that cannot modify POs after issuance.

For either approach we need:
- PO (PDF) with billing contact + remit-to address
- Signed SOW amendment (SOW_v2.docx)
- W9 or equivalent (if remit-to changed)

If you want us to pre-fill portal fields, send the procurement portal link and a contact who will upload. We can prepare the file bundle named: REDWOOD_MERCURY_2029_renewal.zip to match your upload template.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Revenue Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick technical note on capacity uplift and rollout sequence: 

- Recommended uplift: +45% peak concurrency (matches their usage spike). We'll provision a dedicated slot pool on the Dedicated plan for predictable throughput during ramp.
- Lead time: 48–72 hours to provision and smoke-test if we have a signed amendment and PO.
- Fallback policy: if capacity isn't provisioned before go-live, we'll route burst to hosted fallback model (slightly higher per-token cost) to avoid downtime.

Marissa — if Tim can confirm a preferred start date I can block the provisioning window. Also attaching a short ops checklist for the provisioning run.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
